name: HTML <usermedia> element (camera and microphone)
plain: A browser-drawn button that asks for camera or microphone; the click is the request.
meaning: Same power as getUserMedia, but the request starts from a button the site cannot disguise. Aims to cut prompt spam and make recovery after a block possible.

access.prompt_ui: Browser-drawn button with fixed label and icon; click opens the normal camera or microphone prompt.
access.iframe: Needs allow="camera; microphone" in cross-origin iframes

limits.headline: Can ask for camera or microphone through a button the browser draws itself
limits.user_action: You click the browser made Use camera or Use microphone button on the page
can: Show a browser drawn button that starts the camera or microphone request
Let you retry after you blocked access earlier, since the click is a clear request
Open the normal camera or microphone prompt
cannot: Change the button's label or icon to look like something else
Turn the camera or microphone on without your click and approval
Work in Firefox, Safari or iPhone browsers
limits.reach_label: One click, then the usual prompt
limits.differs: Only Chrome, Edge and Chrome on Android support it for now.

story.what_it_is: A browser drawn button that a site cannot fake; clicking it asks for camera or microphone.

marketing.name: Page Embedded Permission Control
marketing.pitch: A proposal for a browser built button so permission requests start from a real click, not a pop up the site fakes.

story.for_you: You see a normal looking button that says something like Use camera. It is drawn by the browser, so the site cannot change what it says. Clicking it starts the permission request, which is clearer than a surprise pop up.
story.for_makers: Makers get a cleaner way to ask, and fewer people who block by mistake because the pop up appeared too early. If someone has blocked the camera, the button lets them change that in one place. It also reduces spam prompts that hurt trust in all sites.

use_cases.example: A call site shows a Use camera button in the pre join screen, and a click is the request, so you know exactly why it is asking.
An ID check page shows a browser drawn camera button so a phisher cannot fake the request to look like your bank.
A browser game with face control shows a clear Enable camera button on the title screen, and not a prompt at page load.
A web camera effect page shows a button for the camera and another for the microphone, so you pick one without a pile of pop ups.
A try on page makes you click Use camera to start the live view, which feels like your choice.
A telehealth waiting room shows the button, so a patient who blocked the camera before can fix it in one click.

risks: Still new and not in every browser

technical_bounds: Cannot be hidden, resized or restyled to deceive
